title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-omar-hassan
content:
Context:
- Hit intermittent GPU OOMs on prod inference nodes (g4dn.12x like, A100-ish behavior). Customer traffic spikes -> some pods crash with CUDA OOM. Repro is flaky locally.

Quick symptoms seen: (copied from logs)
- RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 31.72 GiB total capacity; 30.12 GiB already allocated; 1.77 GiB free; 29.50 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
- cuDNN error: CUDNN_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR
- ImportError: libcudart.so.10.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
- CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version
- WARNING: NVIDIA: GPU device not available (Driver appears not loaded)

Commands run so far (output snippets saved in /tmp/oom-logs-omar/):
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,driver_version,memory.total,memory.used,memory.free --format=csv
  -> driver_version: 510.47 ; memory.used jumps to ~95% during the spike
- nvcc --version && cat /usr/local/cuda/version.txt
- python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.device_count(), torch.version.cuda, torch.backends.cudnn.version())"
  -> True, 4, '11.7', 8200
- ldd `python -c 'import torch;print(torch.__file__)'` | grep libcudart -> shows libcudart.so.11.0 linked, but some containers expect 10.1
- docker inspect --format '{{.HostConfig.Runtime}}' <container> -> runc
- ps aux | grep python ; nvidia-smi pmon -c 1
- dmesg | grep -i nvrm ; journalctl -k | grep -i nvrm
  -> occasional NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus messages during high load (possible driver crash)

Repro attempt (minimal script):
- python repro_alloc.py:
  import torch
  for i in range(200):
      a = torch.randn((1024,1024,64), device='cuda:0')
      b = torch.randn((1024,1024,64), device='cuda:0')
      del a
      torch.cuda.empty_cache()
  # sometimes triggers OOM after ~70 iterations on node X

Hypotheses:
- H1: True OOM from high concurrency + big batch sizes (most likely). Traffic spike caused many concurrent model inferences -> aggregate > GPU memory.
- H2: Memory leak in KV cache (our transformer serving code) where older requests' KV tensors not freed quickly due to hanging references.
- H3: Mismatched CUDA runtime vs driver in some containers/nodes (ImportError: libcudart.so.10.1 + "driver insufficient" errors indicate mixed images). Could explain intermittent behavior across nodes.
- H4: PyTorch/CUDA wheel built for a different libcudnn or ABI; some operations fallback to slower kernels that allocate more temporary memory (less likely but possible).
- H5: Host driver instability causing GPU resets (NVRM messages) and subsequent OOM-like failures reported in userland.

What I tried to mitigate (results):
- Lowered model batch_size from 8->4 at runtime via feature flag: reduced OOM frequency but didn't eliminate.
- Enabled half-precision (fp16) autotune path for one model and memory pressure decreased dramatically for that route.
- Added torch.cuda.empty_cache() in a few code paths (helpful but not root cause).
- Killed and restarted offending container (temporarily fixes until next spike).
- Rolled back a recent runtime package update (which replaced CUDA 11.7 wheel with a 10.1 artifact on a canary node) — that node stabilized.
- Rebuilt image with consistent CUDA runtime libs and pinned torch==2.2.0+cu117 (so wheel matches runtime).

Debug ideas / next steps (todo):
- Capture heap/profile during spike (torch.cuda.memory_snapshot or use nvprof / nsight if possible).
- Add a per-process GPU memory reporter to traces (emit nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY every minute) and attach to traces for correlation with request ids.
- Run small stress test that simulates concurrent inferences to repro reliably (k6 + headless clients).
- Audit Docker images across cluster: grep for libcudart.so.* and compare output to host driver. flag nodes where binary is older/newer than driver supports.
- If driver < required (e.g., runtime built for CUDA 11.7 requires driver >= 515.x), schedule driver upgrade on affected hosts.
- Insert defensive limits in serving layer: per-model concurrent inference cap + queueing + backpressure (reject 429 rather than crash).
- Investigate GC/leaks in KV cache: add weakrefs and force free after request; instrument refcounts in Python to detect retained tensors.
- For debugging segmentation crashes: set CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and enable core dumps; collect backtraces (gdb) when crash occurs.

Useful commands to run on suspect node (one-liners):
- find CUDA libs: ls -l /usr/local/cuda*/lib64/libcudart.so* || true
- check python linked libs: ldd $(python -c "import torch,sys;print(torch.__file__)") | grep cudart || true
- check driver vs runtime: python - <<PY
import torch,sys
print('torch.cuda.version', torch.version.cuda)
print('driver reported by nvidia-smi', end=': ')
import subprocess
print(subprocess.check_output(['nvidia-smi','--query-gpu=driver_version','--format=csv,noheader']).decode().strip())
PY
- list processes using GPU: sudo fuser -v /dev/nvidia* || nvidia-smi pmon -c 1
- check kernel logs for GPU resets: sudo dmesg | egrep -i "NVRM|GPU has fallen off the bus" || true

Notes on driver/runtime mismatch:
- Common symptom: ImportError complaining about a specific libcudart.so.X.Y missing even though a newer libcudart is present -> container was built against older toolkit or path mismatches.
- "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime" typically means the host driver is older than the runtime the binary was built against. E.g., wheel built for CUDA 11.7 may require driver >= 515.
- If host driver is newer but runtime libs are older, you may still have problems (missing symbols). Best practice: build containers with minimal /usr/local/cuda symlink to the toolkit matching the wheel and document required driver version.

Incident breadcrumbs (timeline):
- 2025-02-18 09:12 UTC: First reports from Canary cluster, spikes in memory usage, 3 pod restarts (logs in /tmp/oom-logs-omar/part1).
- 2025-02-19 02:47 UTC: Observed NVRM messages on node-17 -> reimage scheduled but not executed.
- 2025-02-21 14:00 UTC: Rolled back serving-runtime image version v1.14.2 -> OOM frequency decreased on canary nodes.
- 2025-02-24 22:30 UTC: Deployed hotfix restricting per-model concurrency and added metric export for GPU mem.

Quick checklist before escalating to infra team:
- [ ] Collect nvtop/nvidia-smi logs around next incident
- [ ] Compare wheel cuda tag (torch.__version__) vs installed nv driver on node
- [ ] Reproduce with stress script and attach PID to get coredump if crash
- [ ] If driver upgrade is needed, validate on staging images first (document minimum driver required)

Scratch ideas (non-blocking):
- Create a small sidecar process (Go binary) that exposes GPU memory per process via /metrics and can be scraped by Prometheus. Easy to attach and low overhead.
- Use LD_PRELOAD trick to intercept cudaMalloc calls to log large allocations (only for debugging).

Notes to self: keep logs for >48h after next crash. Ask SRE to hold node-17 from automatic upgrades until we capture full repro.

References and quick links I used: (copy/pasted into linked_artifacts above)
- JIRA-INV-3241 (tracking cluster OOMs)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/889 (rollback of cuda artifacts)

End of notes.
